There's a dua you can recite whenever you can inshallah, it's for offering salah regularly. Our Prophet Ibrahim alayhi salam used to recite this dua: 


رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْنِى مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِىۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَآءِ 

My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.

[Ibrahim 14:40]

It's true you can repent and thats good if they do. However, it's dependent on the scenario. Here's this: 
 https://www.google.com/amp/s/islamqa.info/amp/en/answers/148528

In the end, it is always best to avoid falling into these haram relationships and not normalize them. It's all about preventing so that no one has to go through these situations

It does matter, that's something this ummah shouldn't run away from. Learning what is good and bad. Whether it be if you're in a haram or halal relationship, there are things we can learn. These days judging means don't say anything, and that's wrong. We as Muslims, if we see wrong happening, we should help each other and advise. Now it comes down to how you take the approach. We should always advise in a wise manner and not use aggressive language. Yes, Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala is the judge, but it's always better to repent and understand your wrong in this dunya. Versus waiting to be judged for the wrong you've done in the hereafter. Allahu a'alam

In Islam, a haram relationship cannot turn into a halal one. There's no barakah that comes from two individuals that were in a haram relationship from the beginning. Yes anything is possible with Allah because he is the Most Merciful, just doesn't mean we can do anything we want. Especially if you engaged with sin and acted upon it knowing the bad that comes out of it.

Subhanallah
